'''''The Gift''''' is a 2000 American independent [[Southern Gothic]] [[supernatural thriller]] film directed by [[Sam Raimi]] and written by [[Billy Bob Thornton]] and [[Tom Epperson]].<ref name="gingold">{{cite web |last1=Gingold |first1=Michael |title=Review: ''The Gift'' (2000) |url=https://www.fangoria.com/the-gift-review/ |website=[[Fangoria]] |access-date=February 5, 2026 |date=December 20, 2000}}</ref> Thornton and Epperson had written the screenplay for the film prior to the former's 1996 breakout success ''[[Sling Blade]]'', with Thornton taking inspiration from his own mother's alleged [[psychic]] experiences.<ref name ="amelie">{{cite web | author1=Amélie | author2=Sage | title=THE GIFT (2001) | url=http://www.billybobthornton.net/film%20gift.htm | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080303205338/http://www.billybobthornton.net/film%20gift.htm | archive-date= March 3, 2008 | publisher=BillyBobThornton.com | access-date=April 27, 2018}}</ref>

Set in the small [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] town of Brixton, the film focuses on Annie Wilson (portrayed by [[Cate Blanchett]]), a widowed mother and [[clairvoyant]] who operates as a [[fortune teller]] in the rural community to several townsfolk including Buddy Cole (portrayed by [[Giovanni Ribisi]]), a [[mechanic]] struggling with his mental health due to [[Child abuse|abuse by his father]], and Valerie Barksdale (portrayed by [[Hilary Swank]]), a woman in an [[Domestic violence|abusive marriage]] with her hateful, violent [[redneck]] husband Donnie (portrayed by [[Keanu Reeves]]).<ref name="Williamson">{{cite web |last1=Williamson |first1=Graham |title=''The Gift'' (2000) - Sam Raimi's Southern Gothic is Worth Unearthing |url=https://thegeekshow.co.uk/the-gift-2000/ |website=TheGeekShow |access-date=February 5, 2026 |date=May 2, 2025}}</ref>

Annie receives [[psychic]] visions of a gruesome murder and soon finds herself in the town's spotlight when she assists local law enforcement in the [[missing persons]] case of Jessica King (portrayed by [[Katie Holmes]]), the fiancé of the local school's principal Wayne Collins (portrayed by [[Greg Kinnear]]).<ref name="manuel">{{cite web |last1=Manuel |first1=Adrian |title=This Frightening Prestige Thriller Is the Ultimate Forgotten Sam Raimi Film |url=https://www.dreadcentral.com/editorials/437411/this-frightening-prestige-thriller-is-the-ultimate-forgotten-sam-raimi-film/ |website=[[Dread Central]] |access-date=February 5, 2026 |date=September 9, 2022}}</ref>

Filming took place on location around various cities and towns in the [[Savannah metropolitan area]] in the state of Georgia from February to March 2000.<ref name="IMDbFnP">{{cite web |title=''The Gift'' (2000) - Filming & production |url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0219699/locations/ |website=[[IMDb]] |access-date=February 5, 2026}}</ref><ref name="SRFC">{{cite web |author1=Savannah Regional Film Commission |title=20 years ago today, The Gift was released nation wide in theaters! The movie filmed some scenes in Effingham County, Guyton, Savannah, Springfield, and Thunderbolt, GA.  Happy Anniversary! |url=https://www.facebook.com/FilmSavannah/posts/20-years-ago-today-the-gift-was-released-nation-wide-in-theaters-the-movie-filme/10159304614019524/ |website=[[Facebook]] |access-date=February 5, 2026 |date=January 19, 2021}}</ref>

==Plot==
In Brixton, [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]], widow Annie Wilson lives with her three sons. To earn a living, she offers psychic readings to locals. She is friendly with Buddy Cole, an emotionally unstable young man who works at an auto repair shop, and Valerie Barksdale, a woman in an abusive marriage. Valerie's husband Donnie has repeatedly threatened Annie's family because Annie advised Valerie to leave him.

Jessica King, the fiancée of the school principal, Wayne Collins, disappears. After a few days, pressured by Jessica's wealthy father, Sheriff Johnson reluctantly consults Annie. Annie, who is [[clairvoyant]], receives fragmented visions of Jessica's dead body in a pond and several landmarks. Despite his skepticism, Johnson narrows down the location to a pond on Donnie Barksdale's land. The police find Jessica's body there, and Donnie is arrested for her murder.

Buddy, distraught, comes to see Annie. She gives him a washcloth to wipe his face with. Buddy is filled with pain and anger towards his father, and later tries to explain why to Annie, but Annie is preoccupied with the murder and does not listen. That evening, Buddy's mother calls Annie for help, as Buddy has tied his father to a chair. Annie arrives and witnesses Buddy set his father on fire after he reveals that his father [[child sexual abuse|sexually abused]] him as a child. Buddy is arrested and taken to a [[Psychiatric hospital|mental hospital]].

At Donnie's trial, he admits to an affair with Jessica. He is convicted of Jessica's murder and sent to prison. Later, Annie receives more visions revealing Donnie's innocence as well as a premonition of her own death. She asks prosecutor David Duncan to reopen the case and find the real murderer, threatening to reveal his affair with Jessica, to which she was a witness.

Annie confides in Wayne about Donnie's innocence of the murder. At Wayne's suggestion, he and Annie drive out to the pond at night, where Annie has a vision revealing that Wayne is the real murderer. Wayne confesses that he was angry after discovering Jessica was cheating on him with multiple other men including Donnie. Wayne attempts to kill Annie by striking her in the head with a flashlight, but Buddy appears and knocks him out. Annie and Buddy lock the unconscious Wayne in the trunk of Annie's car. Buddy tells Annie that he escaped from the mental hospital, and returns the washcloth she had previously given him.

The two drive to the police station. After encouraging her, Buddy waits in the car while she enters the station. When she returns with the police, Buddy has disappeared. When Annie explains what happened at the pond, Johnson informs her that Buddy died by suicide earlier that day. Annie reaches into her pocket and pulls out the washcloth Buddy returned to her. Annie returns home and looks at photographs of her late husband Ben that her oldest son holds as he falls asleep each night. The next morning, she and her sons visit his grave together.

==Production==
The film was written by Billy Bob Thornton and Tom Epperson before the success of ''[[Sling Blade (film)|Sling Blade]]''.<ref name="Travers" />

==Release==
''The Gift'' was released theatrically in the United States on December 22, 2000, by [[Paramount Classics]].

===Home media===
[[Paramount Home Entertainment]] released ''The Gift'' on VHS and DVD in July 2001.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dvdtalk.com/reviews/2303/gift-the/|work=[[DVD Talk]]|title=Gift, The|last=Beierle|first=Aaron|url-status=live|date=July 13, 2001|archive-date=December 13, 2024|archive-url=https://archive.today/20241213054038/https://www.dvdtalk.com/reviews/2303/gift-the/}}</ref> On December 3, 2024, [[Shout! Factory|Scream Factory]] released a collector's edition [[Ultra HD Blu-ray|4K UHD Blu-ray]] edition of the film,<ref>{{cite web|work=Blu-ray.com|url=https://www.blu-ray.com/news/?id=35540|title=The Gift Collector's Edition 4K Blu-ray|date=November 19, 2024|archive-date=December 13, 2024|archive-url=https://archive.today/20241213054215/https://www.blu-ray.com/news/?id=35540|url-status=live}}</ref> while a 4K UHD Blu-ray is released in the United Kingdom by [[Arrow Films]] on January 27, 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arrowfilms.com/4k/the-gift-limited-edition-4k-ultra-hd/15743064.html|work=[[Arrow Films]]|title=The Gift Limited Edition 4K Ultra HD|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/20241213054400/https://www.arrowfilms.com/4k/the-gift-limited-edition-4k-ultra-hd/15743064.html|archive-date=December 13, 2024}}</ref>

==Reception==
===Critical response===
On [[Rotten Tomatoes]] the film has an approval rating of 58% based on 123 reviews, with an average score of 5.90/10. The site's consensus reads, "With a reported budget of around 10 million, The Gift is obviously a labor of love for those involved. Unfortunately, the A-list cast can't prevent the movie from becoming a by-the-numbers whodunit with an ending that's all but unsatisfactory."<ref>{{Rotten-tomatoes|id=1103231-gift|title=The Gift}}</ref> {{Metacritic film prose|62|29|ref=yes|access-date=September 16, 2025}} Audiences surveyed by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film a grade B on a scale of A to F.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.cinemascore.com/publicsearch/index/title/ |title= GIFT, THE (2015) B  |work= [[CinemaScore]] |url-status= dead |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20180206073531/https://www.cinemascore.com/publicsearch/index/title/ |archive-date= February 6, 2018 }}</ref>

[[Roger Ebert]] gave the film 3 out of 4, and called it "Ingenious in its plotting, colorful in its characters, taut in its direction and fortunate in possessing Cate Blanchett."<ref name="Ebert">{{cite news |date= January 19, 2001 | last= Ebert | first= Roger | author-link= Roger Ebert|title=The Gift | url= https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/the-gift-2001 | work= [[Chicago Sun-Times]]| publisher= [[Sun-Times Media Group]] | location= Chicago, Illinois |via=RogerEbert.com | access-date= April 1, 2020 }}</ref>
Peter Travers of ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' wrote: "Raimi's flair for rich atmospherics — expertly abetted by cinematographer Jamie Anderson ([[Grosse Pointe Blank]]) and composer Christopher Young ([[Wonder Boys]]) — and a cast that goes full throttle hold you in thrall. "<ref name="Travers">{{cite magazine |date=January 19, 2001 |last=Travers |first=Peter |author-link=Peter Travers |title=The Gift |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/movies/movie-reviews/the-gift-103257/ |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] }}</ref>
Todd McCarthy of ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' wrote: "Raimi eschews trendy, over-emphatic effects in favor of a straightforward approach that makes for a solid tale well told."<ref>{{cite web |date=14 December 2000 |first=Todd |last=McCarthy |author-link=Todd McCarthy |title=The Gift |url= https://variety.com/review/VE1117796968 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] }}</ref>

Kenneth Turan of the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' gave it a mixed review and was critical that the "Characters lean too heavily toward the Southern grotesque, and the direction the plot is heading is more predictable than it should be." Despite praising the cast, Turan wrote: "Overly familiar material, even well done, cannot be made more intrinsically interesting than it is. Not even by Cate Blanchett and Keanu Reeves."<ref name="Turan">{{cite news |date=December 20, 2000 |author=Turan, Kennth |author-link= Kenneth Turan |title=Southern Gothic 'Gift' Bears a Mixed Blessing |url= https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2000-dec-20-ca-2144-story.html |newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241214031939/https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2000-dec-20-ca-2144-story.html|archive-date=December 14, 2024|url-status=live}}</ref> A. O. Scott of ''[[The New York Times]]'' wrote: "The picture is saved from mediocrity by Mr. Raimi's smooth competence, and by the unusually high quality of the acting."<ref name= "Scott">{{cite news |date=January 19, 2001 |last=Scott |first=A. O. |author-link=A. O. Scott |title=FILM REVIEW; With Visits From the Dead, a Very Lively Home |url= https://www.nytimes.com/2001/01/19/movies/film-review-with-visits-from-the-dead-a-very-lively-home.html |newspaper =[[The New York Times]]|archive-date=December 14, 2024|archive-url=https://archive.today/20241214032004/https://www.nytimes.com/2001/01/19/movies/film-review-with-visits-from-the-dead-a-very-lively-home.html|url-status=live}}</ref>
Curt Fields of ''[[The Washington Post]]'' called it "So chock-full of stereotypes as to be a filmic Southern Country Safari" and advised "Don't Bother Opening This 'Gift'".<ref name= "washpost">{{cite news |author=Curt Fields |title=Don't Bother Opening This 'Gift' |url= http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/entertainment/movies/reviews/giftfields.htm |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=January 19, 2001|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080820112147/http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/entertainment/movies/reviews/giftfields.htm|archive-date=August 20, 2008|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Box office===
The film grossed $12,008,642 at the U.S. box office against a production budget of $10 million.<ref name= "mojo" /><ref name="numbers" />
